purpose: Reusable quant/dequant baseline adapters and exact-case performance registry
usage: Import quant_baselines under a frontend host NPU guard that encloses torch_npu import and all device use.
Set TORCHINDUCTOR_NPU_BACKEND=ascendc and configure the locked CANN9.1 environment before torch_npu import; use task launch_v16.sh as the verified runtime reference.
Call quant_baselines.make(op,params,original_reference,variant). All data-dependent layout/conversion is inside returned callable.
Cold compilation is outside steady-state performance measurement. fullgraph=True,dynamic=False,suppress_errors=False.
Accept only exact cases present in verified_cases.json; do not infer full family support from a factory.
Use TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 as in the verified v16 launch. CPU parallel precompilation was not used in these measurements.

variant_semantics.torch-eager-control: Original fixed reference; INT4 uses pre-existing verified arithmetic pack instead of AICPU shifts.
variant_semantics.torch-eager-layout-fixed: Small-scale broadcast; required padding and conversions remain timed.
variant_semantics.torch-npu-antiquant: Complete torch_npu.npu_anti_quant API, FP16/BF16 output, FP32 scales unchanged.
variant_semantics.torch-compile-inductor-ascendc: Inductor AscendC graph over Torch expression. May include external device kernels; task counts reported.
variant_semantics.torch-compile-inductor-antiquant: Inductor graph over complete native antiquant wrapper. Native delegation is explicit, not a claim of pureTorch fusion.
variant_semantics.ops-math-native-broadcast: Original Ops-Math Mul graph over actual compact scale broadcasts; complete graph API and layout timed.

selection: Choose lowest same-campaign verified device latency among measured implementations; retain original if faster. Existing published third-party baselines remain historical candidates, not silently removed.
measurement: 3warmups,15independent windows,1GiBflush each,32AIC64AIV; device time from all task records. No host latency claims.
excluded: Raw profiles and payloads are not packaged or uploaded.
Failed correctness variants are not registered; compiler timeouts are not numerical failures.
Website/benchmark page changes are outside this task.

precision.checker: fixed v0.1.0 original CPU oracle and verification rules, including exact quantized codes where required

ops_math_requirements: Original isolated vendor, source manifests, and ARM64/CANN9.1 runtime must match accepted receipts.
Adapter uses original graph.make(MulFwdOp) and retains its per-call descriptors and cleanup.
Its graph factory enables JIT; runner_v15 validates flush buffer on CPU to avoid unrelated aclnnReduceSum initialization failure.
registry_interface: quant_baselines.registry.available(op,case_id,case.params) lists only exact verified variants and rejects same-name parameter mismatches.
quant_baselines.registry.implementations(op,case) returns the existing benchmarks.api.Implementation mapping; use it only inside the host guard and locked runtime.

verify_reference_sources(reference_snapshot_root) checks the included original source snapshot. This partial source snapshot is provenance, not a replacement for the full fixed v0.1.0 workload environment.
Use retained v3 measurement tools to reproduce catalog latencies; generic benchmark callers may use a different timing protocol.
